reviewer: Codex assistant, November 8, 2026; not a human annotator
basis: Four complete public README pages at pinned commits; independently useful semantic corrections only; source text and links as signposts, without fetching linked evidence

events.diagnosis: The product name is used as support for the faster-than-neofetch claim. The page links a benchmark but gives no measured comparison or conditions at this point.
events.minimal_repair: Replace the name-as-evidence rationale with a measured, scoped comparison or point readers to the benchmark; preserve any supported speed claim.

events.quote: Fastfetch has a greater number of features
events.diagnosis: The page lists Fastfetch modules but provides no matched feature inventory or count for Neofetch. The comparative breadth is not established by the command that follows.
events.minimal_repair: Name the comparison set and counts, or state the specific modules available in Fastfetch without an unbounded comparison.

events.quote: has nothing to do with privacy
events.diagnosis: The same answer says local addresses matter on the same network and offers a disable option. The absolute dismissal erases that condition and the user concern.
events.minimal_repair: Scope the statement to nonpublic address routing and keep the same-network qualification and disable instructions; avoid a blanket privacy guarantee.

events.diagnosis: Floating and stacked panes are named, but the page gives no comparison showing those features are unique among terminal workspaces.
events.minimal_repair: List the named pane features without a uniqueness claim, or identify a supported comparison.

events.diagnosis: The introduction explains why local CA management can help development and why manual management is awkward, but does not establish an overall best option for every environment.
events.minimal_repair: State the concrete development tradeoff and mkcert automation without an unqualified ranking.

counterexamples.quote: only actively tested on x86-64 and aarch64 platforms
counterexamples.reason: Explicit test coverage limit is useful.

counterexamples.quote: Fastfetch supports a `Command` module that can run arbitrary shell commands.
counterexamples.reason: Concrete security warning is useful and must be kept.
The CA key warning is necessary.

counterexamples.quote: Adopt only the parts you need.
counterexamples.reason: Scoped adoption advice is useful; no editorial defect was established on this complete page.
